Converts a text file of XYZ triplets on a regular grid, as the ones of the lidar elevation models distributed as text, into a raster: each point becomes the value of the cell centered on it.

**Toolbox folder:** Raster Processing<br>
**Status:** Certified<br>
**Keywords:** Raster, Conversion<br>
**Authors:** Andrea Antonello<br>
**Class:** `org.hortonmachine.modules.Xyz2Raster`

**Inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Unit | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `inFile` | file |  |  | The text file of the XYZ triplets, on a regular grid. |
| `pRes` | Double |  |  | The resolution of the grid of the points, in the units of the coordinates. |
| `pCode` | CRS code |  |  | The code of the coordinate reference system of the points, as authority and number (ex. EPSG:32632). |
| `pSeparator` | String |  |  | The separator of the values, as a regular expression. If not set, any sequence of spaces or tabs. |

**Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `outRaster` | output file |  | The generated raster. |

**Notes**

The points must be the centers of the cells of a regular grid with the given resolution, as written by Raster2Xyz: the bounds of the raster are the ones of the points, enlarged by half a cell. It is not an interpolation: the cells without a point are novalue, and the points that are not on the grid end up in the cell they fall in. To make a raster from scattered points, use SurfaceInterpolator.

The lines that are not three numbers, as a header, are skipped. The values are separated by spaces or tabs, or by the given separator.
